items.title: Lumbar Quadratus Lumborum — Positional Ease
clinicalUse: A person feels a familiar localized ache when rising from a chair or reaching to one side. The question is whether a specific quadratus-lumborum-related tender point can be made comfortably quieter in a shortened position.
Consider only after assessment of mechanical versus non-musculoskeletal pain, neurological features and irritability; a tender point is not a definitive diagnosis.

items.title: Upper Trapezius — Shoulder Girdle Position of Ease
clinicalUse: A patient points to a tender superior shoulder after a long laptop session. Moving the head or lowering a tense shoulder reproduces their familiar ache.
Use as a comfort-based positional trial only when shoulder/neck screening supports a local muscular contribution.

items.title: Infraspinatus Region — Gentle Trigger Point Compression
clinicalUse: A swimmer says reaching across the body feels sore, and gentle palpation of the posterior scapular region reproduces a familiar local discomfort. A tender spot is a clue, not the diagnosis.
Consider a short, tolerable local compression trial only alongside shoulder evaluation and functional exercise.

items.title: Lumbar Paraspinal Soft-Tissue Mobilization
clinicalUse: A patient says their back feels 'locked' after a long day standing. The visible problem might be guarded bending, not a tissue knot waiting to be crushed.
Trial soft-tissue contact as an adjunct to assessment-based movement and exercise rather than diagnosing stiffness by touch alone.

items.title: Gastrocnemius–Soleus Soft-Tissue Mobilization
clinicalUse: A walker reports calf tightness descending steps. Ask what happens during ankle dorsiflexion and stair movement before assuming that the muscle is physically shortened.
May be considered alongside exercise and load management when local muscular sensitivity contributes; assess vascular and tendon conditions first.

items.title: Shoulder Rotation MET — Gentle Isometric Trial
clinicalUse: A patient tries to rotate the shoulder outward to put on a jacket. The arm stops at a comfortable limit; you check whether the problem is irritability, weakness, capsular restriction or another source.
A low-effort shoulder-rotation MET variation may be explored in a medically appropriate and well-screened presentation, alongside active rehabilitation.

items.title: Hip Lateral Glide With Active Flexion — MWM Trial
clinicalUse: A patient says bringing the knee toward the chest is uncomfortable and a squat feels restricted. You establish a safe, reproducible hip-flexion comparable sign.
Consider a selected belt-assisted hip lateral glide only when joint-related pain/mobility impairment is suspected and screening supports a manual trial.

items.title: Thoracic Paraspinal MFR — Broad, Sustained Contact
clinicalUse: A person says their upper back 'feels like cardboard' when twisting to reach the back seat. You check thoracic rotation and rib sensitivity rather than assuming fascia is adhered.
A slow, tolerable soft-tissue contact may be used as a short adjunct when it helps comfortable movement, not as proof of tissue remodelling.
